sections.markdown:
## C — Traffic signals, lane use, sign colors and shapes

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
Signals, signs, and markings keep traffic orderly; cutting through a lot or field to dodge them is illegal, and a police officer's direction overrules every sign and signal [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
Traffic signals bind drivers, motorcycle riders, bicyclists, moped riders, and pedestrians alike [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
At a red light, stop fully at the stop line, or before the intersection or crosswalk where no line exists, and stay stopped while red unless a turn is allowed [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
A right turn on red needs a full stop first, then a both-ways look with the right-of-way yielded to pedestrians and traffic, watching for motorcycles, bicycles, and mopeds [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
No right turn on red is allowed where No Turn on Red signs stand or where a red arrow points right [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
A left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street after a full stop and yield, and never where signs or a red left arrow forbid it [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
A red arrow means stop and stay stopped in that direction unless Right on Red Arrow After Stop or Left on Red Arrow After Stop signs are posted; Virginia otherwise bans turns at red arrows [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
Red-light and red-arrow turn rules differ by state, so learn the local law before turning on red outside Virginia [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
At a flashing red light, stop fully, yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians, and go only when clear; at a railroad crossing, always stop even with no train in sight [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
At a flashing red arrow, stop fully, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and move in the arrow direction only when clear [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A01
A steady yellow light or arrow warns the signal is changing: stop if you have not entered, pass through cautiously if stopping is unsafe or you are already inside, and never speed up [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A01
A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution, marking a spot with higher-than-normal hazard [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A01
At a flashing yellow arrow, turn in the arrow direction when clear, yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians and checking for motorcycles, bicycles, and mopeds [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
At a green light or arrow, go only when clear; turning without a green arrow means yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and letting any pedestrian in the street finish crossing [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A02
When signals show no lights at all, stop and cross as at an all-way stop, unless an officer or authorized person directs traffic or portable stop signs are in use [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A02
Never drive in a lane marked with a red X signal [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A02
A yellow X or yellow diagonal downward arrow means leave that lane as soon as it is safe [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A02
A green arrow opens its lane to driving, while a one-way or two-way turn arrow lets you enter only to turn in the arrow direction [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A02
A pedestrian hybrid beacon runs flashing yellow, then solid yellow, then solid double red with the walk signal while drivers must stop, then alternating flashing reds that release drivers with caution once the crosswalk clears [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A02
A sign's color and shape warn early: shape alone may show in heavy fog, and color reads from far off before the message does [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A02
Red with white means stop, yield, do not, and no; black with white carries regulatory law; yellow with black warns, with a strong yellow-green reserved for school, pedestrian, and bicyclist activity [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A02
Green with white gives destinations, blue with white gives motorist services, brown with white marks historic or cultural interests, orange with black warns in construction zones, and pink with black warns at incidents [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A02
The eight-sided octagon always means stop: halt fully at the sign, line, crosswalk, or curb and wait for a clear way, with every approach stopping at all-way or four-way signs and the left driver yielding on ties [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A02
The triangle means yield: slow down, stand ready to stop, and let vehicles, pedestrians, and bicyclists pass first [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0008]
